entries.originalText: “My Son, when thou feelest the desire of eternal happiness to be poured into thee from above, and longest to depart from the tabernacle of this body, that thou mayest contemplate My glory without shadow of turning, enlarge thine heart, and take in this holy inspiration with all thy desire.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, when you feel the desire for eternal happiness poured into you from above, and long to depart from the tabernacle of this body so that you may contemplate My glory without shadow of turning, enlarge your heart and receive this holy inspiration with all your desire.

entries.originalText: Give most hearty thanks to the Supreme Goodness, who dealeth with thee so graciously, visiteth thee so lovingly, stirreth thee up so fervently, raiseth thee so powerfully, lest thou sink down through thine own weight, to earthly things.
entries.modernizedText: Give heartfelt thanks to the Supreme Goodness, who deals with you so graciously, visits you so lovingly, stirs you up so fervently, and raises you so powerfully, lest you sink down through your own weight to earthly things.

entries.originalText: For not by thine own meditating or striving dost thou receive this gift, but by the sole gracious condescension of Supreme Grace and Divine regard; to the end that thou mayest make progress in virtue and in more humility, and prepare thyself for future conflicts, and cleave unto Me with all the affection of thy heart, and strive to serve Me with fervent will.
entries.modernizedText: For you receive this gift not by your own meditation or striving, but by the gracious condescension of Supreme Grace and Divine regard alone, so that you may make progress in virtue and greater humility, prepare yourself for future struggles, cling to Me with all the affection of your heart, and strive to serve Me with a fervent will.

entries.originalText: “My Son, often the fire burneth, but the flame ascendeth not without smoke.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, often the fire burns, but the flame does not rise without smoke.

entries.originalText: So also the desires of some men burn towards heavenly things, and yet they are not free from the temptation of carnal affection.
entries.modernizedText: So too the desires of some people burn toward heavenly things, and yet they are not free from the temptation of carnal affection.

entries.originalText: Thus therefore they are not acting with an altogether simple desire for God’s glory when they pray to Him so earnestly.
entries.modernizedText: Thus they do not act with an entirely single desire for God’s glory when they pray to Him so earnestly.

entries.originalText: Such, too, is oftentimes thy desire, when thou hast imagined it to be so earnest.
entries.modernizedText: Such too is often your desire, when you have imagined it to be so earnest.

entries.originalText: For that is not pure and perfect which is tainted with thine own self-seeking.
entries.modernizedText: For what is tainted with your own self-seeking is not pure and perfect.

entries.originalText: “Seek thou not what is pleasant and advantageous to thyself, but what is acceptable and honourable unto Me; for if thou judgest rightly, thou must choose and follow after My appointment rather than thine own desire; yea, rather than anything that can be desired.
entries.modernizedText: “Do not seek what is pleasant and advantageous to yourself, but what is acceptable and honorable to Me; for if you judge rightly, you must choose and follow My appointment rather than your own desire, indeed rather than anything that can be desired.

entries.originalText: I know thy desire, and I have heard thy many groanings.
entries.modernizedText: I know your desire, and I have heard your many groanings.

entries.originalText: Already thou longest to be in the glorious liberty of the children of God; already the eternal home delighteth thee, and the heavenly country full of joy; but the hour is not yet come; there remaineth still another season, even a season of warfare, a season of labour and probation.
entries.modernizedText: Already you long to be in the glorious liberty of the children of God; already the eternal home and the heavenly country full of joy delight you; but the hour has not yet come. Another season remains, a season of warfare, labor, and trial.

entries.originalText: Thou desirest to be filled with the Chief Good, but thou canst not attain it immediately.
entries.modernizedText: You desire to be filled with the Chief Good, but you cannot attain it immediately.

entries.originalText: I AM that Good; wait for Me, until the Kingdom of God shall come.
entries.modernizedText: I AM that Good; wait for Me until the Kingdom of God comes.

entries.originalText: “Thou must still be tried upon earth, and be exercised in many things.
entries.modernizedText: “You must still be tried on earth and exercised in many things.

entries.originalText: Consolation shall from time to time be given thee, but abundant satisfying shall not be granted.
entries.modernizedText: Consolation will be given to you from time to time, but abundant satisfaction will not be granted.

entries.originalText: Be strong therefore, and be thou brave both in working and in suffering things which are against thy nature.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore be strong and brave both in working and in suffering things that are against your nature.

entries.originalText: Thou must put on the new man, and be changed into another man.
entries.modernizedText: You must put on the new man and be changed into another man.

entries.originalText: Thou must often do what thou wouldst not; and thou must leave undone what thou wouldst do.
entries.modernizedText: You must often do what you would not and leave undone what you would do.

entries.originalText: What pleaseth others shall have good success, what pleaseth thee shall have no prosperity.
entries.modernizedText: What pleases others will succeed, while what pleases you will not prosper.

entries.originalText: What others say shall be listened to; what thou sayest shall receive no heed.
entries.modernizedText: What others say will be listened to; what you say will receive no attention.

entries.originalText: Others shall ask and receive; thou shalt ask and not obtain.
entries.modernizedText: Others will ask and receive; you will ask and not obtain.

entries.originalText: Others shall be great in the report of men, but about thee shall nothing be spoken.
entries.modernizedText: Others will be great in the report of men, but nothing will be said about you.

entries.originalText: To others this or that shall be entrusted; thou shalt be judged useful for nought.
entries.modernizedText: This or that will be entrusted to others; you will be judged useful for nothing.

entries.originalText: “For this cause nature shall sometimes be filled with sadness; and it is a great thing if thou bear it silently.
entries.modernizedText: “For this reason nature will sometimes be filled with sadness, and it is a great thing if you bear it silently.

entries.originalText: In this and many like things the faithful servant of the Lord is wont to be tried, how far he is able to deny himself and bring himself into subjection in all things.
entries.modernizedText: In this and many similar things the faithful servant of the Lord is tested, to see how far he can deny himself and bring himself into subjection in all things.

entries.originalText: Scarcely is there anything in which thou hast need to mortify thyself so much as in seeing things which are adverse to thy will; especially when things are commanded thee to be done which seem to thee inexpedient or of little use to thee.
entries.modernizedText: There is scarcely anything in which you need to mortify yourself so much as in seeing things opposed to your will, especially when you are commanded to do things that seem unwise or of little use to you.

entries.originalText: And because thou darest not resist a higher power, being under authority, therefore it seemeth hard for thee to shape thy course according to the nod of another, and to forego thine own opinion.
entries.modernizedText: And because, being under authority, you dare not resist a higher power, it seems hard to direct your course according to another’s nod and to give up your own opinion.

entries.originalText: “But consider, My Son, the fruit of these labours, the swift end, and the reward exceeding great; and thou shalt find it no pain to bear them then, but rather the strongest solace of thy patience.
entries.modernizedText: “But consider, My Son, the fruit of these labors, their swift end, and the exceedingly great reward; then you will find it no pain to bear them, but rather the strongest comfort for your patience.

entries.originalText: For even in exchange for this trifling desire which thou hast readily forsaken, thou shalt always have thy will in Heaven.
entries.modernizedText: For even in exchange for this small desire that you have readily given up, you will always have your will in Heaven.

entries.originalText: There verily thou shalt find all that thou wouldst, all that thou canst long for.
entries.modernizedText: There truly you will find all that you would have, all that you can long for.

entries.originalText: There thou shalt have all good within thy power without the fear of losing it.
entries.modernizedText: There you will have every good within your power without fear of losing it.

entries.originalText: There thy will, ever at one with Mine, shall desire nothing outward, nothing for itself.
entries.modernizedText: There your will, always one with Mine, will desire nothing outward and nothing for itself.

entries.originalText: There no man shall withstand thee, none shall complain of thee, none shall hinder, nothing shall stand in thy path; but all things desired by thee shall be present together, and shall refresh thy whole affection, and fill it up even to the brim.
entries.modernizedText: There no one will oppose you, no one will complain of you, no one will hinder you, nothing will stand in your path; but all the things you desire will be present together and will refresh your whole affection and fill it to the brim.

entries.originalText: There I will glory for the scorn suffered here, the garment of praise for sorrow, and for the lowest place a throne in the Kingdom, for ever.
entries.modernizedText: There I will give glory for the scorn suffered here, the garment of praise for sorrow, and for the lowest place a throne in the Kingdom forever.

entries.originalText: There shall appear the fruit of obedience, the labour of repentance shall rejoice, and humble subjection shall be crowned gloriously.
entries.modernizedText: There the fruit of obedience will appear, the labor of repentance will rejoice, and humble subjection will be gloriously crowned.

entries.originalText: “Now therefore bow thyself humbly under the hands of all men; nor let it trouble thee who said this or who ordered that; but take special heed that whether thy superior, thy inferior, or thy equal, require anything from thee, or even show a desire for it; take it all in good part, and study with a good will to fulfil the desire.
entries.modernizedText: “Now therefore bow yourself humbly under the hands of everyone; do not let it trouble you who said this or who ordered that, but take special care that whether your superior, your inferior, or your equal requires anything of you, or even shows a desire for it, you receive it all gladly and strive with a willing heart to fulfill the desire.

entries.originalText: Let one seek this, another that; let this man glory in this, and that man in that, and be praised a thousand thousand times, but rejoice thou only in the contempt of thyself, and in Mine own good pleasure and glory.
entries.modernizedText: Let one seek this and another that; let one glory in this and another in that, and be praised a thousand thousand times, but rejoice only in contempt of yourself and in My own good pleasure and glory.

entries.originalText: This is what thou art to long for, even that whether by life or by death God may be ever magnified in thee.”(1)
entries.modernizedText: This is what you should long for: that whether by life or by death God may always be magnified in you.”(1)
